required_floor_classes.lane_definition: An income-security/family scenario cannot pass if eligible households lose benefit access, childcare access, enrollment access, language/disability access, or timely payment access below reviewed floors.
An income-security/family scenario cannot pass if lower costs are achieved by degrading benefit accuracy, childcare quality, casework quality, appeals, due process, or family safety.

An income-security/family scenario cannot pass if benefit loss, childcare burden, work-transition burden, or administrative burden shifts to children, lower-income households, disabled people, single parents, rural families, or high-need groups without reviewed distributional evidence.
An income-security/family scenario cannot pass if child poverty, material hardship, food security, housing stability, childcare continuity, or recession resilience falls below reviewed floors.

An income-security/family scenario cannot pass without a benefit package, take-up model, federal/state/local translation, administration cost, work-transition model, childcare capacity model, behavior model, and incidence model.

income_security_family_specific_floor_de.definition: Child poverty and deep child poverty require sourced baseline, policy, and stress values before any lower-cost scenario can pass.
Material hardship, food security, housing stability, and utility hardship require explicit sourced floor values.
Formal childcare access, affordability, supply, quality, and geographic availability require explicit reviewed floors.
Work incentives, care responsibilities, transition cliffs, benefit phaseouts, and employment stability require explicit behavior and distributional review.
Benefit package design, take-up, timeliness, administration, appeals, federal/state/local delivery, and compliance burden require sourced values.

public_warning_phrases: This income-security/family floor packet defines required floor concepts, but it does not set threshold values or pass/fail findings.

No lower-cost income-security/family scenario is admissible until child poverty, material hardship, childcare access, work/care transition, equity, adequacy/resilience, and delivery-feasibility floors are thresholded, sourced, reviewed, and passed.
A benefit concept is not a benefit package model, take-up model, federal/state/local translation, federal score, target cost, or solver input.
No target cost, federal effect, gross savings, net savings, solver input, department-cut instruction, technology-savings claim, or balanced-budget claim is populated.
No FOIA request, records request, form, email, phone call, or agency/person contact was submitted.

This record is not outcome-floor passage, not a benefit package model, not a take-up model, not a federal score, not a target-cost selection, not solver input, not a solver run, not a rate calculation, not a public rate card, not a tax proposal, not a savings estimate, not a waste finding, not a fraud finding, not a department-cut instruction, not a technology-savings claim, and not a balanced-budget claim.
